data.title: mTORC1 inhibition upregulates CD20 and enhances anti-CD20 antibody efficacy in B-cell precursor acute lymphoblastic leukemia
data.authors: Dąbkowska A, Janowska M, Pastorczak A, Domka K, Nowicka Z, Urbanska Z, Zając W, Bugajewski M, Grzybowska J, Pruchniak P, Fidyt K, Fendler W, Taslim J, Crump NT, Ushmorov A, Patkowska E, Firczuk M

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.model_system: BCP-ALL cell lines; patient-derived and in vivo models
data.finding: mTORC1 inhibitors upregulate CD20 via the AKT-FOXO1 axis and promote B-lineage maturation in B-cell precursor ALL, enhancing the antitumor efficacy of anti-CD20 monoclonal antibodies -- including in high-risk IKZF1-deleted disease -- providing a rationale for combining mTORC1 inhibition with CD20-directed immunotherapy.
data.abstract_excerpt: B-cell precursor acute lymphoblastic leukemia (BCP-ALL) is characterized by impaired B-cell maturation and poor prognosis in relapsed/refractory (R/R) cases. While CD20-targeted immunotherapies offer clinical benefit, their efficacy is limited by low and heterogeneous CD20 expression on BCP-ALL cells. In this study, we demonstrate that overexpression of wild-type IKZF1, a tumor suppressor frequently mutated in high-risk BCP-ALL, upregulates CD20 and promotes leukemic B cell maturation.
